overview: Formally known as the Alliance to Restore the Republic, the Rebel Alliance is a large coalition of factions opposed to the Galactic Empire. It maintains a Civil Government with six ministries and a Military arm comprising Fleet Command, SpecForce, Starfighter Command, Intelligence, and Support Services, all under Mon Mothma as Chief of State with dictatorial wartime powers that automatically terminate upon the Emperor's fall. The Alliance is chronically outgunned and outmanned, relying on cell networks, guerrilla tactics, and the courage of beings from hundreds of species.
short_descriptor: Committed and underresourced. Their greatest strength is that they've already decided what they're willing to lose. Don't underestimate what that does to a person's decision-making.

witness_statement.text: I served on an Imperial frigate for six years. Thought the Rebels were terrorists — that's what they told us in the briefings. Then we hit a supply convoy near Sullust and I watched a medical frigate with no weapons hold position so three transports full of refugees could jump to hyperspace. They knew they were dead. They held anyway. I put in my resignation the next rotation.
witness_statement.source: Former Imperial naval officer, surrendered to Alliance Sector Force

history.heading: FOUNDATION
history.text: The resistance began during the Clone Wars when Senators Mon Mothma (Chandrila), Bail Organa (Alderaan), and Garm Bel Iblis (Corellia) watched Palpatine consolidate emergency powers. They met secretly at Organa's Cantham House residence on Coruscant, developing means and methods for public and private resistance. Organa played the loyalist front to gain access to Imperial committees; Mothma pressed for direct action; Bel Iblis was a harsh critic of Imperial rule.

history.heading: EARLY RESISTANCE
history.text: Outside the Senate, armed resistance fighters appeared early in Imperial history but were isolated and easily suppressed. Bail Organa secretly supported Alderaanian resistance forces. Conditions worsened as more species were enslaved and worlds subjugated, pushing more citizens toward resistance. Garm Bel Iblis's wife and daughters were killed by Imperial assassins; he escaped into hiding to build a militia. When Mon Mothma's arrest became imminent, Organa tipped her off and she escaped to personally organize resistance forces.

history.heading: THE CORELLIAN TREATY
history.text: Two years before the Battle of Yavin, a Force-user called Starkiller saved Senator Organa and convinced the conspirators to formally unite. The Corellian Treaty was signed, creating the Alliance to Restore the Republic. Darth Vader disrupted the signing ceremony but the conspirators escaped. Mon Mothma became Commander-in-Chief and wrote the Declaration of Rebellion.

history.heading: DECLARATION OF REBELLION
history.text: The Declaration initially worked too well -- several star systems immediately seceded from the Empire. These Secession Worlds were quickly retaken but transferred significant cash, materials, manpower, and starships to the Alliance first. For roughly two years after the Declaration, recruitment was slow but steady against formidable Imperial propaganda.

history.heading: AFTER YAVIN
history.text: After the Battle of Yavin, the Rebels abandoned Yavin 4 immediately and currently operate without a primary secret base. High Command operates from the Rebel Fleet and occasional temporary bases while searching for a new permanent base location.

how_they_operate.heading: THE CIVIL GOVERNMENT
how_they_operate.text: The Civil Government mirrors a typical large-scale civilian government with six Cabinet ministries: Education (propaganda, intelligence, infiltration monitoring), Finance (tax collection, Alliance Credit issuance at roughly 25% standard credit value), Industry (manufacturing, secret corporate deals), State (diplomacy, external negotiations), Supply (feeding and equipping all Alliance forces), and War (translating policy into military commands).

how_they_operate.heading: THE MILITARY
how_they_operate.text: The Alliance Military is split into Alliance Forces (not attached to any sector, deployed as needed) and Sector Forces (serving specific sectors with semi-autonomous control). Key commands include: Alliance High Command (Supreme Allied Commanders), Fleet Command (the single most vital military asset), Intelligence (largest command with galaxy-wide agents), Starfighter Command (most useful and sought-after resource), Special Forces Command (approximately ten divisions of elite SpecForce troops), and Support Services (logistics, medical, safe worlds).

how_they_operate.heading: THE FLEET
how_they_operate.text: The Alliance Fleet comes from defections, Allied Commands, purchases, theft of Imperial assets, and allied shipyards like Mon Calamari. There are no standardized Rebel capital ships. Mon Mothma heavily restricts fleet use, detaching up to 25% of ships on rotating basis for raids. Task forces typically consist of frigates, corvettes, and gunships, with heavily-armed freighters filling many roles.

how_they_operate.heading: GROUND FORCES
how_they_operate.text: Sector Forces contain the bulk of ground troops as regular and irregular forces, typically fighting with guerrilla warfare tactics. SpecForce includes seven regiments: Marines/SpaceOps, Pathfinders, Urban Guerrillas, Wilderness Fighters, Infiltrators, Heavy Weapons Specialists, and Technicians.

how_they_operate.heading: INTELLIGENCE & CELLS
how_they_operate.text: Cell networks operate on staunch Imperial worlds using three-person cells with blind upward connections. Orders flow down; intelligence flows up through blind drops. Alliance Intelligence has three divisions: Operations (field agents, infiltration, sabotage, spying), Intentions (analysis, interrogation, code-breaking), and Counterintelligence (detecting Imperial infiltration).

how_they_operate.heading: TACTICS
how_they_operate.text: Common tactics include: cell networks for clandestine operations, commando raids and SpecForce operations for surgical strikes, fleet detachment raids (limited scale), starfighter strikes (the most common and classic tactic), sabotage coordinated with military operations, and hit-and-fade attacks. Retreat is built into Rebel battle planning. Terrorism is expressly forbidden by Mon Mothma and the Alliance Council.

motivations_legacy: Restore the Republic and representative galactic government supported by the people
End the Empire's subjugation of species and abuse of citizens
Overthrow the Emperor and dismantle the Empire
Free all beings in the galaxy from Imperial tyranny
Counter institutionalized slavery, wrongful imprisonment, genocide, and repression
Reclaim the right of free beings to remove oppressive government from power

secondary: Free all beings from Imperial tyranny
motivations.notes: The Alliance's ideological commitment to democracy and freedom is genuine but creates operational tension — Mon Mothma holds dictatorial wartime powers while fighting to restore democratic governance. The diversity of motivations among member factions (revenge, independence, idealism, pragmatism) is both a strength and a source of internal friction.

strategic: Destroy the Galactic Empire and restore representative galactic government
Unite all species under a new Republic modeled on the Old Republic's ideals
Build a military force capable of challenging Imperial supremacy
Win the propaganda war by demonstrating that the Empire can be defeated
operational: Recruit skilled personnel — pilots, engineers, doctors, intelligence agents — from across the galaxy
Secure starships, weapons, and supplies through any available channel: defections, purchases, theft, allied manufacturing
Maintain cell network security on Imperial-controlled worlds
Conduct guerrilla operations that degrade Imperial capability without overextending Alliance resources

avoided: Terrorism — expressly forbidden by Mon Mothma and the Alliance Council
Holding territory through conventional occupation — Operation Domino proved the Alliance lacks the manpower
Large-scale fleet engagements — Mon Mothma restricts fleet deployment to rotating 25% detachments
methods.notes: The Alliance fights an asymmetric war. Starfighter strikes are the signature tactic. Cell networks provide intelligence and sabotage capability on Imperial worlds. SpecForce conducts surgical operations. Retreat is built into every battle plan. The Alliance avoids any action that could be characterized as terrorism, since Imperial propaganda already paints them as terrorists.

strengths: Extraordinary species diversity provides access to unique skills, perspectives, and worlds across the galaxy
Ideological commitment produces highly motivated personnel willing to take extreme personal risks
Alliance Intelligence is the largest command, with galaxy-wide agent networks providing constant information flow
Mon Calamari shipyards provide a dedicated allied manufacturing base for capital ships
Cell network architecture limits damage from any single security breach
weaknesses: Chronic shortage of starships, personnel, weapons, medical supplies, and materiel persists at every organizational level from cell networks to Fleet Command.
The Alliance Credit trades at approximately 25% of standard Imperial credit value, severely limiting purchasing power on the open market.
Allied Commands and Sector Forces operate with semi-autonomous authority, producing conflicting operational priorities that High Command lacks the leverage to fully resolve.
The absence of standardized capital ships means every vessel in the fleet requires unique maintenance procedures, spare parts, and crew training.

The Alliance lacks the manpower to hold territory after capturing it, as demonstrated by the failure of Operation Domino, forcing reliance on hit-and-fade tactics that cede strategic initiative to the Empire.

behavior_under_threat.low: Increase Intelligence monitoring. Reposition cell network contacts. Prepare evacuation contingencies for nearby bases.
behavior_under_threat.medium: Activate SpecForce assets for reconnaissance. Begin relocating sensitive personnel and equipment. Alert Sector Force commanders.
behavior_under_threat.high: Execute evacuation protocols for threatened bases. Commit starfighter squadrons for cover operations. Intelligence shifts to active counterintelligence mode.
behavior_under_threat.critical: Full base evacuation. Fleet assets provide covering withdrawal. Scatter personnel to pre-designated rally points. Destroy all records and equipment that cannot be moved. Survival of personnel takes absolute priority over materiel.

alert_escalation.notes: Cell networks use blind drops and cutouts, which adds latency but protects the chain. Intelligence flows up; orders flow down. No single captured operative can compromise more than their immediate cell. In emergency situations, field commanders have significant autonomy to act without waiting for High Command authorization.

tension_patterns: Starfighter Command and Sector Forces regularly compete for the same limited squadron assets, as Alliance fleet resources are insufficient to support simultaneous operations.
Alliance Intelligence vetting procedures are compressed by recruitment urgency, producing cleared personnel whose backgrounds contain unresolved gaps.
Operational necessity frequently requires partnerships with smugglers and criminal contacts whose methods contradict the Alliance's stated principles against exploitation.

Allied Commands and High Command issue conflicting operational directives to the same field units, reflecting the structural tension between semi-autonomous sector operations and centralized strategy.
Successful military operations that produce civilian collateral damage provide Imperial propaganda with material that undermines Alliance recruitment and public sympathy.

mcguffin_interest_legacy.reason: Alliance Intelligence is enormously important to day-to-day operations. The Alliance constantly seeks military and civilian intelligence on Imperial weaknesses, future intentions, base locations, fleet movements, and code-breaking opportunities.

The Alliance is chronically short of starships, starfighters, heavy military equipment, medical supplies, food, and transport vessels. Ordnance and Supply constantly seeks ships and gear through defections, purchases, allied manufacturing (Mon Calamari shipyards), and outright theft of Imperial assets.

Recruitment of skilled individuals -- pilots, engineers, doctors, intelligence agents, military officers -- is critical. Mon Mothma personally negotiates with resistance groups to bring them into the Alliance. Imperial defectors (individuals, starship crews, even planetary governments) are actively sought.

mcguffin_interest.notes: The Alliance desperately needs intelligence data (fleet movements, base locations, code-breaking material), military hardware (starships, weapons, supplies), skilled personnel (pilots, engineers, defectors), and any technology that could offset Imperial numerical superiority. Jedi artifacts are of secondary interest but fall under Special Operations.

territory.name: Rebel Fleet (mobile)
territory.notes: Alliance High Command currently operates from the Rebel Fleet after abandoning Yavin 4. The fleet is the Rebellion's most important military asset.

territory.name: Yavin 4 (former main base)
territory.notes: Massassi Temple complex on the fourth moon of gas giant Yavin. Housed thousands of troops, up to four starfighter squadrons. Abandoned immediately after the Battle of Yavin.

territory.name: Dantooine (former base)
territory.notes: Used as main base before Yavin 4. Abandoned after discovery of an Imperial tracking device.

territory.name: Chandrila
territory.notes: Homeworld of Mon Mothma. Core World with a thriving agrarian society. Serves as a recruiting ground but suffers Imperial retaliation through tariffs and political arrests. Still under Imperial governorship.

territory.name: T-Star 2
territory.notes: Code name for a safe world in Wild Space, spinward of the tail end of the Corellian Run. Population about 5,000, mostly humans with some Wookiees. Also holds an Imperial prisoner colony of about 400.

territory.name: Brigia (former)
territory.notes: Temporary main base in the Tion Cluster. Forced to flee during Operation Strike Fear.

territory.name: Scattered secret bases galaxy-wide
territory.notes: The Alliance maintains a network of secret bases ranging from recon field bases and caches to full sector force headquarters. Includes outposts, safe-houses, medical stations, and starfighter bases in environments from caverns and jungles to asteroids and ocean depths.

prominent_figures.name: Mon Mothma
prominent_figures.notes: From Chandrila. Former Republic and Imperial Senator. Co-founder of the Alliance alongside Organa and Bel Iblis. Wrote the Declaration of Rebellion. Personally negotiates with resistance groups to bring them into the Alliance. Expressly forbids terrorism. Only person to have held the Chief of State position.
prominent_figures.network_assessment: Mon Mothma holds dictatorial wartime powers over the Alliance and uses them with restraint, which is why the coalition hasn't fractured. She's the only reason a hundred different resistance groups point in the same direction.
prominent_figures.wants: Restoration of the Republic through military victory over the Empire. Maintaining Alliance unity long enough to achieve it.
prominent_figures.secret: Her dictatorial authority automatically terminates upon the Emperor's fall — she designed the position with a built-in expiration to prevent the Alliance from becoming what it fights against.

behavior.under_pressure: Becomes more diplomatic, not less. Draws factional leaders into shared decision-making to distribute both responsibility and commitment.
behavior.when_losing: Accepts tactical losses to preserve strategic assets. Will sacrifice territory, equipment, and bases before she'll sacrifice personnel unnecessarily.
behavior.loyalty: Loyal to the ideal of the Republic, not to any individual or faction. She'll make unpopular decisions if they serve the larger cause.
behavior.tells: When Mon Mothma personally contacts a resistance group rather than delegating, the Alliance needs something specific that only that group can provide.

useful_to_players: Her prohibition on terrorism means the Alliance won't support operations that target civilians — but it also means they're predictable in what they'll accept
Her personal negotiation style means resistance groups can appeal directly to her if they have something valuable to offer
The Alliance under her leadership values skilled individuals — pilots, engineers, doctors — and will invest resources in recruiting them
hooks: Mon Mothma just dispatched personal envoys to three Outer Rim sectors simultaneously. When she recruits that actively, the Alliance is preparing something large.
Word is she turned down a Hutt offer for a weapons shipment. The Alliance needs weapons badly, which means the strings attached were worse than the shortage.

prominent_figures.name: Bail Organa
prominent_figures.notes: Led Alderaan to become a pacifist world after the Clone Wars. Played the loyalist front to gain access to Imperial Senate committees. Secretly supported Alderaanian resistance forces. Resigned from the Senate after the Corellian Treaty signing; his daughter Leia took his place. Killed in the destruction of Alderaan.
prominent_figures.network_assessment: Bail Organa built the Rebellion's foundations while sitting in the Imperial Senate. He played the loyalist for years while funding resistance forces with Alderaanian resources. Dead now — killed with his planet. His legacy is the Alliance itself.
prominent_figures.wants: Was driven by the preservation of democratic governance and the protection of his people. Both objectives ended at Alderaan.
prominent_figures.secret: He maintained secret connections to surviving Jedi, including Obi-Wan Kenobi, and knew the true parentage of Luke and Leia Skywalker.

behavior.under_pressure: Maintained his loyalist cover with extraordinary discipline. Years of operating under Imperial scrutiny without breaking character.
behavior.when_losing: Accepted personal risk to protect others. Resigned from the Senate to protect his daughter's cover as his replacement.
behavior.loyalty: Loyal to Alderaan, to the Republic ideal, and to the people he personally committed to protecting — including the Skywalker children.
behavior.tells: Historical pattern: Organa's charitable donations spiked whenever he was channeling resources to the Rebellion through Alderaanian relief funds.

useful_to_players: His network of contacts and safe houses still exists even after his death — Alderaanian survivors carry his legacy and his debts of honor
His daughter Leia inherited both his Senate seat and his resistance network, making her the living continuation of his work
Alderaan's destruction radicalized thousands who previously sat on the fence — Organa's martyrdom is a recruiting tool the Alliance still uses
hooks: An Alderaanian relief fund account that Organa set up before his death is still active. Someone is drawing on it — either a surviving cell or someone who cracked the access codes.
A cargo manifest from one of Organa's last shipments turned up in a smuggler's haul near Sullust. Whatever he was moving, it never reached its destination.

prominent_figures.name: Princess Leia Organa
prominent_figures.notes: Daughter of Bail Organa. Replaced her father in the Imperial Senate. Participated directly in operations against the Empire. Should have a seat on the Advisory Council representing Alderaan but elects to serve in other roles.
prominent_figures.network_assessment: Leia operates at every level of the Alliance — diplomatic, operational, and tactical. She'll negotiate a supply deal in the morning and run a blockade in the afternoon. Underestimate her range and you'll miss what she's actually doing.
prominent_figures.wants: Destruction of the Empire that killed her father and her planet. She channels grief into operational effectiveness.
prominent_figures.secret: She declines her Advisory Council seat to maintain operational flexibility — a politician on the council is constrained; a field operative is not.

behavior.under_pressure: Becomes sharper and more decisive. Pressure clarifies her priorities rather than clouding them.
behavior.when_losing: Refuses to accept defeat as final. Captured by the Empire, she resisted interrogation and maintained cover on operational details.
behavior.loyalty: Loyal to the Alliance cause and to the memory of Alderaan. Personal relationships are subordinated to the mission but never abandoned.
behavior.tells: When Leia volunteers for a mission rather than delegating, the stakes are personal. She doesn't risk herself casually.

useful_to_players: Her diplomatic credentials give her access to systems and contacts that military operatives cannot reach
Her willingness to work directly with field operatives means she can authorize resources and make decisions without bureaucratic delay
Alderaanian survivors are fiercely loyal to her — invoking her name carries weight in certain circles
hooks: Princess Leia was spotted on a diplomatic shuttle heading to a neutral system that the Alliance has never operated in before. She's opening a new channel.
An Imperial bounty on Leia just doubled. Someone in the Empire wants her badly enough to spend serious credits, which means she's close to something important.

prominent_figures.name: Garm Bel Iblis
prominent_figures.notes: From Corellia. Harsh critic of Imperial rule. His wife and daughters were killed by Imperial assassins. Escaped into hiding and built a militia. Feared Mon Mothma's potential for dictatorial ambition. Laid groundwork for a dozen Rebellion cells over 20 years.
prominent_figures.network_assessment: Bel Iblis is a co-founder who doesn't fully trust the organization he helped create. He built a dozen cells over twenty years and runs his own militia. He's Alliance, but he's his own Alliance.
prominent_figures.wants: The Empire destroyed — but not at the cost of replacing it with another centralized authority. He watches Mon Mothma's power as carefully as he watches the Emperor's.
prominent_figures.secret: His distrust of Mon Mothma's dictatorial authority is deep enough that he maintains independent command structures and supply lines separate from Alliance High Command.

behavior.under_pressure: Fights with the discipline of a professional soldier who has been fighting for twenty years. Calm, methodical, and relentless.
behavior.when_losing: Falls back to prepared positions. His militia is trained for extended guerrilla campaigns, not last stands.
behavior.loyalty: Loyal to Corellia, to the Republic ideal, and to the memory of his murdered family. Not loyal to any individual leader, including Mon Mothma.
behavior.tells: When Bel Iblis stops attending Alliance coordination meetings, he's about to conduct an operation that he doesn't want High Command to know about in advance.

useful_to_players: His independent militia operates outside standard Alliance channels, making him accessible to groups that don't have formal Alliance connections
His distrust of centralized authority means he sympathizes with independent operators and small resistance cells
His twenty years of cell-building means he knows safe houses, dead drops, and contacts across a dozen sectors
hooks: Bel Iblis pulled his militia out of a joint operation last week without explanation. Either he doesn't trust the intelligence or he doesn't trust the commander.
A Corellian freighter captain was asking about Bel Iblis by name at a waystation near Selonia. That's either a recruitment approach or a trap — and knowing which matters.

prominent_figures.name: Admiral Ackbar
prominent_figures.notes: Mon Calamari commander. Oversaw Project Shantipole in the Roche asteroid field, developing the B-wing starfighter with the Verpine to counter Imperial Nebulon-B frigates. Promoted to Admiral after defending the prototypes from an Imperial strike force.
prominent_figures.network_assessment: Ackbar commands the Alliance Fleet — the single most important military asset the Rebellion has. He's a tactical thinker who earned his rank through combat, not politics. When the fleet moves, he's the reason it moves correctly.
prominent_figures.wants: Naval superiority sufficient to engage Imperial forces in open battle. The B-wing program was his first step toward evening the odds.
prominent_figures.secret: His experience as a former slave of Grand Moff Tarkin gave him intimate knowledge of Imperial naval doctrine and command psychology that informs every tactical decision he makes.

behavior.under_pressure: Analytical and controlled. Calculates odds continuously and will order withdrawal the moment the math no longer favors engagement.
behavior.when_losing: Executes fighting retreats with precision. Preserving the fleet is always the priority — ships lost cannot be replaced easily.
behavior.loyalty: Loyal to Mon Calamari, to the Alliance, and to the crews who serve under him. He takes fleet casualties personally.
behavior.tells: When Ackbar requests detailed intelligence on a system's gravity wells and hyperspace entry points, he's planning an operation there.

useful_to_players: His fleet command authority means he can authorize naval support for operations that serve Alliance strategic interests
His tactical caution means Alliance naval assets won't be risked on operations with unclear intelligence — provide solid data and he'll commit resources
Mon Calamari shipyard connections give him access to repair and refit capabilities that the rest of the Alliance lacks
hooks: Ackbar just dispatched a frigate to survey a system that's been flagged as an Imperial staging area. If he's risking a capital ship on reconnaissance, the target is significant.
The Admiral has been in extended communication with the Verpine at Roche. Project Shantipole produced the B-wing — a second collaboration could shift the balance again.

prominent_figures.name: Luke Skywalker
prominent_figures.notes: Destroyed the Death Star at the Battle of Yavin, instantly becoming a Rebel hero. One of the Alliance's only known Force-using allies after Obi-Wan Kenobi's death.
prominent_figures.network_assessment: Skywalker destroyed the Death Star and that makes him the most visible Rebel in the galaxy. He's also an untrained Force-user, which makes him a magnet for Inquisitors and Vader personally. Being near him is both an asset and a liability.
prominent_figures.wants: Understanding of the Force and his place in the conflict. His motivations are still forming — he's driven by instinct and conviction more than strategy.
prominent_figures.secret: His connection to the Force makes him a priority target for the Inquisitorius and Darth Vader specifically, for reasons that go beyond his military value to the Alliance.

behavior.under_pressure: Acts on instinct, often with results that defy tactical logic. His Force sensitivity gives him reaction speed and situational awareness that compensate for his lack of formal training.
behavior.when_losing: Refuses to abandon allies. His loyalty to individuals overrides tactical calculation, which is both inspiring and operationally dangerous.
behavior.loyalty: Intensely loyal to friends, to the Alliance, and to the memory of Obi-Wan Kenobi and his family on Tatooine.
behavior.tells: When Skywalker goes quiet and withdrawn, he's processing something through the Force. When he becomes suddenly certain about a course of action, he's acting on feelings he can't fully articulate.

useful_to_players: His hero status means invoking his name carries weight with Alliance personnel and sympathizers across the galaxy
His Force abilities make him invaluable for operations that require unconventional solutions or against Force-sensitive threats
His inexperience means he's approachable and willing to work with small teams and independent operators in ways senior Alliance leadership would not
hooks: Skywalker was seen leaving the fleet alone in his X-wing with no filed flight plan. He does that sometimes — follows feelings to places the Alliance doesn't know about yet.
Imperial chatter about Skywalker has shifted from 'wanted terrorist' to 'priority acquisition target.' Someone in the Empire wants him alive, and that changes the threat profile.

prominent_figures.name: Ahsoka Tano
prominent_figures.role: Fulcrum agent, former Jedi Padawan, covert intelligence operative
prominent_figures.notes: Former Padawan of Anakin Skywalker who left the Jedi Order before its fall. Operates under the codename Fulcrum, coordinating rebel cells and gathering intelligence. One of the most capable Force users still active, though she no longer considers herself a Jedi.
prominent_figures.network_assessment: If she contacts you, the mission is real and the stakes are high. She does not waste time on operations that don't matter. Trust the intel she provides — she has sources we cannot replicate.
prominent_figures.wants: Coordination of disparate rebel cells into an effective resistance network while maintaining operational security against Imperial intelligence.
prominent_figures.secret: Ahsoka is aware of Darth Vader's true identity as her former master Anakin Skywalker. This knowledge drives her operations against the Inquisitorius with particular urgency.

behavior.under_pressure: Draws on decades of combat experience. Prioritizes the safety of allies over personal risk. Will engage Inquisitors directly to protect others.
behavior.when_losing: Executes precise tactical withdrawal. Uses Force abilities to cover retreat. Will sacrifice escape routes to ensure others get out.
behavior.loyalty: To the principles the Jedi were supposed to represent, not to any institution. Personal bonds with former Clone Wars allies remain strong.
behavior.tells: Speaks more carefully when she senses Force-related danger. Instinctively positions herself between threats and non-combatants.

useful_to_players: Fulcrum intelligence channels can provide mission-critical information unavailable through any other source.
hooks: A message came through on the Fulcrum channel. No details, just coordinates and a time. That's how she operates.
Someone matching her description was seen leaving the Inquisitor's compound. Whatever she found in there, she took it with her.

prominent_figures.name: Captain Rex (CT-7567)
prominent_figures.role: Veteran clone trooper commander, rebel military advisor
prominent_figures.notes: One of the few clone troopers who removed his inhibitor chip before Order 66. Served under General Skywalker during the Clone Wars. Now serves as a military advisor to Phoenix Cell, bringing decades of tactical experience against both Separatist and Imperial forces.
prominent_figures.network_assessment: Rex knows Imperial military doctrine because he helped build it. His tactical assessments of garrison behavior are the most reliable in the network. If he says a position is indefensible, believe him.
prominent_figures.wants: Protection of remaining clone trooper survivors and effective application of Clone Wars combat experience to the current rebellion.
prominent_figures.secret: Rex maintains contact with other clones who removed their chips. The size and locations of this informal network are unknown to Alliance command.

behavior.under_pressure: Reverts to Clone Wars combat training — precise, disciplined, coordinated. Commands any available allies as if they were trained soldiers.
behavior.when_losing: Executes fighting withdrawal by the book. Prioritizes wounded and non-combatants. Will hold a position alone to buy time.
behavior.loyalty: To his brothers and to the people who earned his trust through action. Institutions have failed him before.
behavior.tells: Uses clone trooper hand signals unconsciously. Checks sight lines and exit routes upon entering any space.

useful_to_players: Rex can identify Imperial unit types, estimate garrison strength, and predict standard Imperial tactical responses from minimal observation.
hooks: Old clone showed up at the outpost yesterday. Doesn't say much, but the way he looked at the Imperial patrol — he was counting them, timing them, mapping them.
Rex says the garrison commander is running a Marg Sabl maneuver. Nobody else here knows what that means, but Rex is already moving equipment.

prominent_figures.name: Lando Calrissian
prominent_figures.role: Smuggler, gambler, entrepreneur, reluctant rebel ally
prominent_figures.notes: A charming con artist and skilled pilot who moves between legitimate business and criminal enterprise with equal ease. Currently building contacts across the Outer Rim. His loyalty is complicated — he looks out for himself first, but has been known to risk everything for the right cause or the right person.
prominent_figures.network_assessment: Calrissian is useful precisely because he is not committed. He moves in circles we cannot access. The price is that his cooperation is always conditional and his information always serves his interests first.
prominent_figures.wants: Personal profit and the accumulation of legitimate business holdings that provide both wealth and social respectability.
prominent_figures.secret: Lando is quietly building a network of contacts and resources that could support either side of the conflict, positioning himself to prosper regardless of outcome.

behavior.under_pressure: Talks his way out first. Deploys charm, deception, and negotiation in rapid sequence. Violence is a last resort but he is capable when pushed.
behavior.when_losing: Looks for the deal. Will offer information, services, or future favors to avoid a loss. Always has an escape route planned.
behavior.loyalty: To himself and a small circle of personal friends. Can be moved by genuine appeals but will not sacrifice himself for a cause.
behavior.tells: Straightens his cape when he's about to lie. Becomes more charming when he's most nervous.

useful_to_players: Lando's social connections span criminal syndicates, legitimate businesses, and Imperial bureaucracy — he can open doors no one else can.
hooks: Calrissian just won a mining operation in a sabacc game. Either he's the luckiest man in the galaxy or the other player wanted him to have it.
Lando says he can get us past the blockade. He also said that about Kessel, and that didn't go well for anyone.

enemies: COMPNOR (Commission for the Preservation of the New Order)
Certain ex-Separatist factions allied with Imperial interests
Some Quarren factions (prior to Mon Calamari's open rebellion)
allies: Mon Calamari (openly joined after Battle of Yavin; provide shipyards and starships)
Bothans (growing unofficial pro-Rebellion faction; skilled spies and information brokers)
Sullustans (significant contingent serving the Alliance; focused on operations inside SoroSuub Corporation)
Wookiees (enslaved species sympathetic to the Alliance)
Chandrila (homeworld of Mon Mothma; covert support despite Imperial retaliation)
Incom Corporation engineers (defected design team responsible for the X-wing)
Verpine (assisted in developing the B-wing starfighter at the Roche asteroid field, though officially neutral)
Various sympathetic planetary governments providing covert donations of labor, starships, materials, and equipment
Former Secession Worlds (transferred significant resources to the Alliance before being retaken)

relationship_notes.imperial_military: The primary military adversary. The Alliance fights an asymmetric war against vastly superior Imperial forces.
relationship_notes.imperial_security_bureau: The ISB hunts Rebel cells relentlessly. Alliance Intelligence and ISB Counterintelligence are locked in a constant shadow war.
relationship_notes.black_sun: Complex — Black Sun's slave trading and criminal operations are antithetical to Alliance values, but some Vigos (Lonay, Sprax) supply weapons and materials to desperate Rebel Sector Forces.
relationship_notes.hutt_cartel: Pragmatic. The Alliance dislikes Hutt slavery and exploitation but sometimes operates in Hutt Space where Imperial authority is weaker. Neither side trusts the other.
relationship_notes.mon_calamari: The most important allied military asset. Mon Calamari shipyards produce capital ships for the Alliance fleet.

regional_presence_legacy.notes: The Outer Rim is where Rebel support is greatest. Remote worlds are more likely to resist Imperial rule. Key assets include the Mon Calamari system (openly allied), former Yavin 4 base, scattered sector force headquarters, and numerous outposts. The Atrivis sector was an early stronghold where multiple resistance groups united.

Highly dangerous operating environment with strong Imperial support. Chandrila provides covert support and recruiting. Alderaan was a key base of operations until its destruction. Cell networks operate on staunch Imperial worlds. Coruscant (Imperial Center) hosted the original Cantham House conspiracy.
Mixed presence; some flashpoint areas with increasing Rebel attacks. Bestine area noted as a flashpoint.
Several Rebel safe worlds are located in Wild Space, including T-Star 2. These remote locations protect refugee populations and serve as sanctuaries.
A few safe worlds are located near or within the edge of the Unknown Regions, selected for extreme remoteness to prevent accidental discovery.

source_material_notes: The Age of Rebellion Core Rulebook (pages 385-416) is the definitive source, covering Alliance history, civil government, military structure, bases, tactics, and adversary profiles. Desperate Allies expands on Alliance politics and diplomacy. Dawn of Rebellion provides pre-ANH context on the Alliance's formation.
